bus_and_suppression_boundary.consequence: Span's missing physical repin explains why its rlog cannot establish production suppression topology; it does not by itself erase stock-CAN1 traffic from logical bus 1. B6's segment-level absence therefore remains a bounded observation, while its producer side and suppression point remain open until a relay-correct LTA transition capture is obtained.

bus_and_suppression_boundary.diagnostic_vs_interception: ELM327 param=1 + logical bus 1 attaches FDCAN2 to the normal harness CAN1 wires and is sufficient for direct/passive observation. A physical CAN0/CAN1 repin is still required to move that network onto the CAN0/CAN2 relay pair for normal comma interception, stock-source suppression, and side-of-relay producer attribution.
bus_and_suppression_boundary.public_route_observation: The directly reusable 0x00F/0x025/0x0AA/0x101/0x116/0x176 state evidence in the public TSS3 route is on logical bus 1. That bus also exposes exact-H/F search-vocabulary 0x0D7 and 0x030, but not B6 or H/F's 0x351/0x394/0x4A3/0x4C8 Tx set.

span_moving_observation.field_context: The maintainer reports Span had not physically swapped the Toyota-B CAN0/CAN1 pairs for this log.
span_moving_observation.interpretation: Panda harnessStatus=flipped is USB-C harness orientation, not the Toyota-B physical CAN0/CAN1 repin. ELM327 param=1 keeps logical bus 1/FDCAN2 on the normal harness CAN1 wires, so an unmodified harness can passively observe that unsplit network. The missing physical repin prevents CAN0/CAN2 relay interception and camera-side-vs-car-side producer attribution; it does not by itself make stock CAN1 traffic invisible to logical bus 1.

bus_and_suppression_boundary.toyota_b_harness_fact: Official Toyota-B hardware uses CAN0/CAN2 as the intercept-relay pair and CAN1 as a separate unsplit network. Panda harnessStatus=flipped is cable orientation, not a physical Toyota-B CAN0/CAN1 repin.

aging.boundary: These are exact classifier/latch counter thresholds. Counter wall-clock meaning is not asserted here, and the paired states are not renamed temporary/permanent.

0x01.selection: populated in the exact-H event table but not consumed by recovered accumulator 0x4B692

0x02.lifetime: primary latch uses calibration 200 and additionally requires FEBEE8B0 >= 17736 before clearing; secondary latch uses calibration 600
0x02.selection: class-2 primary active => state 6 while secondary bit FEBE7F5D[0] is set, else state 7

0x04.lifetime: primary latch uses calibration 200 and additionally requires FEBEE8B0 >= 17736 before clearing; shared secondary latch uses calibration 600
0x04.selection: class-4 primary active => state 8 while secondary bit FEBE7F5D[1] is set, else state 9

0x08.selection: class-0x08 counter/bit selects state 13 when the additional 0x4B7AA condition permits; otherwise the classifier can fall through to state 16

0x0F.selection: class-0x0F counter/bit selects state 14 when the additional 0x4B7AA condition permits; otherwise the classifier can fall through to state 16

0x20.selection: class-0x20 counter/aggregate bit is one direct state-11 cause

0x80.selection: class-0x80 counter blocks the deepest state-0 normal path; state 16 is a general fallback and is not unique to class 0x80

0xF0.selection: supported by 0x4B692 and the state-11 branch, but no exact-H event-table row currently carries class 0xF0

public_route_vs_exact_h_f_visibility.boundary: The public route exposes 0x00F and 0x0D7 but no 0x0B6, and only 0x030 from the exact-H/F five-PDU Tx set. Because the route has no carFw/F181 join, this cannot prove B6 is feature-gated or absent on an exact H/F EPS bus; it instead proves the route is not evidence of a complete exact-H/F EPS-bus mirror.

can_0x030_b6_bit1.classification: Q-axis actual-current-derived debounced status; exact H's threshold detector is calibration-disabled
can_0x030_b6_bit1.exact_h_calibration_effect: feature flag 0x5A makes the BB8F6 detector's enabled-only set branch unreachable and forces its raw detector output FEBEB64D to zero on each execution; debounce calibration is zero. This closes the physical source family and detector-disable state, not an OEM display name for the final debounced bit.
can_0x030_b6_bit1.openpilot_consequence: Do not treat B6[1] as a generic steering-ready/authority bit. Its source is motor Q-current monitoring and its exact-H detector is disabled by calibration.

span_observation.boundary: Span's moving rlog is not exact-F181-joined and therefore cannot override exact-H calibration identity; its 0/1 variation is useful cross-specimen evidence only.

can_0x351_force7.classification: independent severe/special status override, distinct from the C159B49-linked 0x351 base electrical-monitor code path
can_0x351_force7.openpilot_consequence: Treat the force-7 indication as a distinct conservative fault/status input if 0x351 becomes available, but do not rename it C159B49 or map it to temporary/permanent without dynamic policy evidence.

record_aggregate_side.aggregate: 0x36CEC ORs each valid record's +6 ushort into one aggregate (plus FEBE720E under its recovered gate)
record_aggregate_side.boundary: The exact source geometry and bit are closed; an OEM/DTC name for record +6 bit15 is not recovered from the current corpus.
record_aggregate_side.mode_table: FEBE6F94[24] selects one of two 12-byte record banks rooted at FEBE6FC8 or FEBE70E8

status_bitmap_side.boundary: FEBE6FB4 is a broad internally consumed 16-bit status bitmap; current static evidence does not assign Toyota names to bits0/1.
chain: 0x36AAA stores it at FEBE6FB4 with XOR-redundant mirrors FEBE6ED0/FEBE6ED2

can_0x351_force7.wire_effect: 0x46E62 forces the 0x351 status code to 7 and sets FEBE7DD1=1

exact_h_f_visibility.boundary: The moving Span rlog exposes 0x00F/0x0D7 but no B6, and only 0x030 from the exact-H/F five-PDU Tx set. Because all Panda-state samples are ELM327 param=1, logical bus 1 was attached to the normal harness CAN1 wires throughout; lack of the physical CAN0/CAN1 repin therefore blocks interception/side attribution rather than passive CAN1 observation. B6 absence is still only a segment-level negative: no stock-LTA off->active->off transition or exact F181 join is present, so feature/request gating and specimen/segment differences remain open.

harness_observation_boundary.field_context: The maintainer reports Span had not physically swapped the Toyota-B CAN0/CAN1 pairs for this log.
harness_observation_boundary.interpretation: Panda harnessStatus=flipped is USB-C harness orientation, not the Toyota-B physical CAN0/CAN1 repin. ELM327 param=1 keeps logical bus 1/FDCAN2 on the normal harness CAN1 wires, so an unmodified harness can passively observe that unsplit network. The missing physical repin prevents CAN0/CAN2 relay interception and camera-side-vs-car-side producer attribution; it does not by itself make stock CAN1 traffic invisible to logical bus 1.

tss3_fd_network.0x18A_disposition: 0x18A is one 64-byte ~20-Hz member of the broader 0x180..0x18B family and lies inside comma's older TSS2 radar-track namespace. That makes radar/object semantics a concrete competing prior to the community lateral-control label; neither interpretation is promoted until producer/field/authentication dataflow is independently joined.
tss3_fd_network.interpretation: The same 22-ID/DLC FD network geometry appears in the public 2023 route, the older Span capture, and Span's independently supplied moving/driving rlog. The moving rlog upgrades persistence of this geometry beyond NRtD/static conditions, but still does not assign field semantics, producer ownership, or command roles.
